mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the cost of capital for firms, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of months with FEDFUNDS below 4.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market boosting corporate profits and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >60% of triggered instances, or t-test p-value >0.05 vs baseline returns.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust consumer demand and housing activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Joint growth in RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict positive 20-day returns in >60% of cases, with Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals manufacturing supply constraints, reducing corporate output and increasing input costs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of INDPRO decline periods, or Rank IC > 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% for three months signals aggressive monetary tightening, reducing corporate borrowing and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of months with PAYEMS growth, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion (GDP growth >2.5% annualized), stretched valuations cause S&P 500 underperformance, leading to negative returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of GDPC1 growth >2.5% periods, or Rank IC > 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals broad economic slowdown, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Joint decline in INDPRO and HOUST fails to predict negative 20-day returns in >60% of cases, with Rank IC < 0.03.
